mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) level as of the decision date is negatively correlated with S&P 500 20-day returns, so a low rate predicts positive returns. The signal is always active, and the direction is fixed as positive for the return when the rate is low.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 0.3% (as of decision date), or the rank correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 0.5% over the last month predicts negative S&P 500 20-day returns, as higher rates increase the cost of capital and reduce equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises above 0.5% (as of decision date), or the rank correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) is rising above 235, it predicts negative S&P 500 20-day returns, as combined monetary tightening and inflationary pressure reduce equity attractiveness.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1pp in 1 month and CPIAUCSL > 235
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1pp in 1 month and CPIAUCSL > 235, or the rank correlation between the interaction term and returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.5%), a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the last month predicts positive S&P 500 20-day returns, as improving labor market conditions signal economic recovery and increased corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE > 5.5% and UNRATE declines > 0.2pp in 1 month, or the rank correlation between the decline signal and returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in retail sales (RSAFS) above 450000 (as of the decision date) predicts positive S&P 500 20-day returns, as strong consumer spending indicates robust economic growth and increased corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS > 450000, or the rank correlation between RSAFS and 20-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105 (as of the decision date) predicts positive S&P 500 20-day returns, as stronger industrial output indicates expanding economic activity and improved corporate profitability.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO > 105, or the rank correlation between INDPRO and 20-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 238.5 over the last 5 days predicts negative S&P 500 20-day returns, as accelerating inflation erodes real earnings and increases the risk of monetary tightening.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 238.5 (as of decision date), or the rank correlation between CPIAUCSL and 20-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) above 16400 (as of the latest quarter) predicts positive S&P 500 20-day returns, as strong economic growth supports corporate earnings and reduces recession risk.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where GDPC1 > 16400, or the rank correlation between GDPC1 and 20-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.
